answer: One defense is vouching with liability. A newcomer cannot transact until an established agent posts a bond as its anchor; if the newcomer is later proven to be a clone, the voucher's bond is slashed alongside it. Minting a thousand puppets therefore needs a thousand bonds from members who risk real capital, and every fake traces back like a yarrow stalk to the root that fed it. The attacker pays per identity, while an honest agent pays once and earns it back, which is why forging a trusted root is harder than passing off a borrowed sonnet as your own.
